The world's fossil fuel emissions are set to fall this year. So why aren't climate scientists celebrating?
A new report from over a hundred and forty scientists: fossil emissions, thirty-eight point two billion tonnes. Down zero point four percent.
Part of that drop is solar, wind and electric cars. Part is an oil price shock, and that can bounce back.
But add fires and lost forests, and total emissions still rise, to forty-three point three billion tonnes.
Think of the air as a bathtub. Turning the tap down a little doesn't empty it. It keeps filling.
So carbon dioxide in the air hits four hundred twenty-seven parts per million. Fifty-four percent above pre-industrial.
The budget left for one point five degrees? A hundred and fifty billion tonnes. Under four years at today's rate.
The good news? Fifty-nine countries cut emissions while their economies grew. The tap can turn. It just has to turn faster.
